tools.name: subscribe_events
tools.title: Event stream connection
tools.description: Returns a protected event stream connection descriptor and replay cursor for recorded liquidation cascades and wall changes, without opening a connection.

after.description: Optional opaque, exclusive event cursor for this symbol and tier.

tools.name: get_liquidation_census
tools.title: Liquidation census
tools.description: Returns aggregate liquidation price bands, venue coverage and snapshot age from the Hyperliquid position census, with no individual account rows.

tools.name: desk_read
tools.title: Desk read
tools.description: Returns served liquidation levels, state and reasons for one symbol from the Desk Read wall snapshot, with deprecated verdict compatibility fields.

lang.description: Optional. Language of lines, text and act_label. Default en.

pull.line: Bigger wall: above, $286M at $80,821, 0.90% away. Nearest: $16M 1.20% below.

crowd.line: Longs are paying 0.03% per funding interval and open interest is up 4.0% today.

output_example.flags_basis: liq_distance_pct: the closest wall's distance from price in percent, from one per-side wall set (the near cell, the band wall, or the labeled ladder fallback). wall_within_1pct: that same distance is under one percent. crowd_aligned: the funding side the crowd pays on agrees with the pull direction; null without a funding read. Descriptive, never a recommendation.
output_example.verdict_rule: verdict reads the same wall set as flags: wall_in_band when the nearest wall on either side is under 1 percent from price (the emitted liq_distance_pct), no_wall_in_band when walls exist but none is that close, thin_data when there is no price or no wall data. verdict_long and verdict_short apply the same test to that side's losing-side wall only (below for a long, above for a short) and add the liquidation distance of a hypothetical entry at the current price and assumed_leverage, or of your position when you send one. Descriptive, never a recommendation: proceed, reduce and skip are no longer emitted.

reasons: losing-side wall below at 1.20% ($16M at $80,335), not inside 1%
losing-side wall above at 0.90% ($286M at $80,821), inside 1%

output_example.deprecated_note: The verdict, stop and target fields are deprecated compatibility fields, never advice. verdict is descriptive (wall_in_band, no_wall_in_band or thin_data) and reads the same wall set as the descriptive flags liq_distance_pct, wall_within_1pct and crowd_aligned, which replace it. stop_suggestion and target_suggestion mirror the deprecated plan and render on no customer surface.
lines: Bigger wall: above, $286M at $80,821, 0.90% away. Nearest: $16M 1.20% below.
Longs are paying 0.03% per funding interval and open interest is up 4.0% today.
output_example.text:
Bigger wall: above, $286M at $80,821, 0.90% away. Nearest: $16M 1.20% below.
Longs are paying 0.03% per funding interval and open interest is up 4.0% today.

_meta.verdict_compatibility_contract: The deprecated compatibility field verdict is wall_in_band, no_wall_in_band or thin_data, never null; proceed, reduce and skip are no longer emitted (contract change, SDK 0.4.1 docs). wall_in_band means the nearest wall on either side is under 1 percent from price, the same distance as flags.liq_distance_pct and the same test as flags.wall_within_1pct; thin_data means no price or no wall data. verdict_long and verdict_short apply that test to the losing-side wall (below for a long, above for a short) at the current price and assumed_leverage, or for your position. confidence is null with confidence_basis unscored until the public ledger scores verdicts. Compatibility metadata includes verdict_side, verdict_long, verdict_short, verdict_other, bias and confidence. The verdict, stop and target fields are deprecated compatibility fields, never advice. verdict is descriptive (wall_in_band, no_wall_in_band or thin_data) and reads the same wall set as the descriptive flags liq_distance_pct, wall_within_1pct and crowd_aligned, which replace it. stop_suggestion and target_suggestion mirror the deprecated plan and render on no customer surface.

tools.name: hk_levels
tools.title: Liquidation levels
tools.description: Returns hk.levels.v1 liquidation levels from Bybit perpetual walls, with snapshot age, delay and evidence labels, using six Free coins delayed by 2 hours without a key.

tools.name: get_proof_summary
tools.title: Public proof summary
tools.description: Returns the public proof summary with sample sizes, confidence bounds and evidence links from the published scorecard and feed reconciliation record.

tools.name: get_magnet_levels_teaser
tools.title: Public wall clusters
tools.description: Returns the three largest liquidation clusters per side for BTC and ETH from the public delayed wall snapshot.

symbol.description: Optional: BTCUSDT or ETHUSDT (the free-teaser majors). Omit for both.

tools.name: get_feed_trust_summary
tools.title: Public feed audit
tools.description: Returns venue verdicts, match rates, coverage and sample counts from the public liquidation feed reconciliation audit.

tools.name: get_liquidation_magnets
tools.title: Liquidation magnets
tools.description: Returns per horizon liquidation magnets and historical reach rates with sample sizes and confidence bounds from the published calibrated record.

frame.description: Optional horizon filter: 15m | 1h | 4h | 1D. Omit for all horizons.

tools.name: get_reach_stats
tools.title: Historical level reach
tools.description: Returns historical band reach rates by symbol and horizon with sample sizes and confidence intervals from the walk forward record.

tools.name: get_feed_trust
tools.title: Feed reconciliation
tools.description: Returns per venue verdicts, coverage and sample counts for the service's liquidation feed from its recorded reconciliation checks.

venue.description: Optional venue filter (e.g. binance, bybit, okx, deribit). Omit for all.

tools.name: get_accuracy_proof
tools.title: Published track record
tools.description: Returns the published track record with sample sizes, baselines and measurement windows from the same aggregate as the public proof page.

tools.name: get_engine_read
tools.title: Engine read
tools.description: Returns unvalidated directional context for a symbol and horizon from the customer engine read payload as descriptive context, not a forecast.

tools.name: get_proof_anchors
tools.title: Daily proof anchors
tools.description: Returns dates, content digests and chain hashes from the public daily proof anchor ledger, excluding private signatures and signing keys.

limit.description: Optional: how many of the most recent daily anchors to return (default 30, max 200).

tools.name: get_decision_packet
tools.title: Evidence packet
tools.description: Returns liquidation magnets, historical reach, venue structure and feed trust from the existing evidence readers, with unavailable components labeled.

tools.name: prepare_trade
tools.title: Position calculation
tools.description: Returns position quantity, notional and optional gross reward to risk from user supplied levels and an evidence packet, without placing or signing an order.

tools.name: list_symbols
tools.title: Supported symbols
tools.description: Returns six Free coins without a key or the supported symbol allowlist with a key, including the applicable delay.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.title: Prepaid credit checkout
tools.description: Creates and returns a Stripe Checkout URL for a selected prepaid data credit pack from the configured catalog, leaving payment completion to the user.

return_url.description: Optional hunterkiller.io URL to return to.

tools.name: feedback
tools.title: Service feedback
tools.description: Stores the caller's service feedback and returns its receipt using the same validation and internal review queue as the public feedback form.

need.description: What you needed and did not get (required).

context.description: Optional. What you were trying to do.

symbol.description: Optional. Perp pair this is about.

tool.description: Optional. The tool or endpoint this is about.

contact.description: Optional. Where a human can reply.
